articles.title: Short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children represents a significant and growing global health burden. This study aims to report the short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted to assess outcomes in pediatric patients with various types of hemodialysis access. This prospective cohort study included all consecutive pediatric patients with ESRD who presented to the Vascular and Endovascular Surgery Department at a tertiary hospital from October 2022 to October 2023. RESULTS: The study included 50 pediatric patients, with a mean age of 10.5 ± 5.7 years. The cohort was predominantly female 35 (70%), while males accounted for 15 (30%) The overall technical success rate remained high at 45 (90%). The failure rate was 5 (10%). CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that pediatric arteriovenous fistulas (predominantly autogenous), when carefully planned and executed, can achieve high primary success and patency rates, with manageable complications in children with end-stage renal disease.

articles.title: Maternal kidney disease and composite kidney outcomes in the offspring.
articles.abstract: Maternal chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its relationship with long-term offspring kidney health remains uncertain. This retrospective maternal-child cohort study examined whether maternal CKD or reduced kidney function before or during pregnancy was associated with a composite kidney outcome in offspring. Live births in the Taiwan Mother and Child Health cohort from 2007 to 2017 were followed through 2018. In the primary cohort, maternal kidney disease was defined as claims-based CKD meeting chronicity criteria before or during pregnancy; the maternal eGFR subcohort additionally included eGFR-defined reduced kidney function. The primary outcome comprised ICD-defined CKD, reduced eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or ≥30% eGFR decline at age ≥2 years, or kidney replacement therapy. Laboratory components were interpreted as reduced kidney function rather than definitive CKD unless diagnostic chronicity was documented. Models adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, offspring, and perinatal covariates. Among 79,036 children, 4,687 (5.9%) met the composite kidney outcome. Maternal kidney disease was associated with modestly higher odds of the composite outcome (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.00-1.66) and offspring all-cause mortality (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.15-3.09). Analyses of individual components of the composite outcome, sex-stratified subgroups, and trimester-specific exposure windows were exploratory, imprecise, and not adjusted for multiplicity. Maternal CKD or reduced kidney function may identify dyads who warrant long-term kidney surveillance, although causal pathways require confirmation.

articles.title: Prevalence of Fabry disease GLA variants among patients with parapelvic cysts: a Multicenter Italian Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fabry disease is a rare X-linked disorder characterized by the accumulation of sphingolipids in various vital systems, leading to multiple organ damage. As previous data showed the association between Fabry disease and parapelvic cysts, the aim of our work was to evaluate the prevalence of GLA variants in patients with parapelvic cysts. METHODS: From November 2022 to September 2024, we conducted a multicenter cohort study on patients referred to 15 Italian Nephrology Units. The prevalence of GLA variants among patients with parapelvic cysts was compared to the prevalence of Fabry disease in newborns and in chronic kidney disease (CKD )patients. RESULTS: Among 306 enrolled patients with parapelvic cysts, we identified seven different variants in the GLA gene in eight patients (4 females, 4 males) (1.3%, 1.3%, respectively): three patients with two different pathogenic variants (2 males, 1 female) (0.65%, 0.32%, respectively), two patients with variants of uncertain significance (VUS) (2 males) (0.65%) and three with benign variants (3 females) (0.98%). The overall prevalence of GLA variants in our population was 2.6%, which is 11-fold higher than in CKD patients not on dialysis (ND) (0.24%), and this difference resulted statistically significant (P <.0001; 11.07, 95%CI: 4.89; 25.06). Our results showed a prevalence of GLA variants 200 times higher compared to Italian newborn screening programs. CONCLUSION: Our study is the first to analyze the prevalence of GLA variants in patients with parapelvic cysts, showing results that are significantly higher compared to CKD-ND patients and the general population. Parapelvic cyst identification, even before clinical manifestations, is crucial for early Fabry disease diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Outcomes Following Kidney Failure From IgA Nephropathy Compared to Diabetic Kidney Disease and Other Glomerular Diseases.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a major cause of kidney disease worldwide, yet contemporary comparative outcome data following kidney failure are limited. We compared trends in access to kidney transplantation and mortality among patients with kidney failure due to IgAN, to those with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) or other glomerular diseases (GD). STUDY DESIGN: Longitudinal cohort study. SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients with kidney failure initiating maintenance dialysis (1965-2023) due to IgAN, DKD, or other GD in Australia. EXPOSURE: Kidney failure etiology. OUTCOMES: All-cause death, death from cardiovascular disease and cancer, and entry onto the deceased donor kidney transplant waitlist. ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Age-standardized incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates and temporal trends assessed using log-linear regression-derived estimated annual percentage change (EAPC). Associations between kidney failure etiology and outcomes estimated using inverse probability treatment-weight (IPTW)- adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: 44,659 patients (4,925 with IgAN; 15,079 with other GD; 24,655 with DKD) were studied with a median follow-up of 53 months (IQR 23.3-109.8). The age-standardized incidence of IgAN remained stable over the past two decades (EAPC -0.01%, 95% CI - 0.80 to 0.78). Compared with other GD, patients with IgAN experienced lower all-cause (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.65-0.73; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.60-0.74; p < 0.001) mortality, and increased rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.39-1.73; p < 0.001). Compared with IgAN, patients with DKD had higher all-cause (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.53-1.64, p<0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.71-1.91, p<0.001), lower cancer-related mortality (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95, p=0.009), and lower rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.60-0.69, p<0.001). LIMITATIONS: Residual confounding, diagnostic misclassification due to variation in biopsy practices. CONCLUSION: Differences in survival and placement onto the kidney transplant waitlist exist across patients with different etiologies of kidney failure. Individuals with IgAN have longer survival and enter the transplant waitlist more often than those with DKD or other GD.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: Nursing Activities Score in critically ill patients on invasive mechanical ventilation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: to assess the association between invasive mechanical ventilation duration, classified as prolonged and non-prolonged, and nursing workload in critically ill patients. METHOD: a prospective cohort study with adult patients on mechanical ventilation for up to 21 days or more. Nursing workload was measured using the Nursing Activities Score (NAS). Clinical data were collected using a structured questionnaire. A significance level of 5% was adopted. RESULTS: considering 61 patients, there was no significant difference in nursing workload between prolonged and non-prolonged mechanical ventilation according to NAS [111.2 (105.118) vs. 111.8 (107.119); p=0.880], nor was there an association between mechanical ventilation time and this score (AUC=0.512). Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with vasoactive drugs (96%; p=0.007) and greater severity of acute kidney injury (KDIGO=3.78%; p=0.009). CONCLUSION: mechanical ventilation duration was not associated with changes in nursing workload, which remained high regardless of the ventilatory support duration.

articles.title: Feasibility of a machine learning model for predicting weight gain after kidney transplantation machine learning and weight gain after kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Excessive weight gain after kidney transplantation adversely affects patient and graft outcomes. Machine Learning has been increasingly used to improve risk prediction across a range of transplant-related outcomes, yet its application to post-transplant weight trajectories remains unexplored. This study is the first to evaluate the feasibility of using Machine Learning algorithms to identify predictors of weight gain after kidney transplantation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. We developed an Elastic Net regression model with 10-fold cross-validation to predict body weight variation at 12 months post-transplant. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. RESULTS: Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. CONCLUSIONS: This pioneering study establishes an analytical benchmark and reveals the informational limits of standard clinical datasets for predicting post-transplant weight gain. While Machine Learning application is feasible, current demographic and clinical variables are insufficient for precise individual prediction. Future models must integrate more granular behavioral and pharmacological data to achieve clinically actionable risk stratification.
authors: de Freitas Júlia de Melo Cardoso

articles.title: Prevalence and Impact of Popliteal Artery Injury Associated with Knee Dislocations, Ligament Injuries, and Peri-Knee Fractures: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmission Database, 2016-2020.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe knee trauma, including knee dislocations, ligament injuries, and peri-knee fractures, carries a risk of popliteal artery injury (PAI). We aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical impact of PAI in adult patients sustaining severe knee trauma. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult inpatients (≥18 years) with peri-knee fracture, knee dislocation, or ligament injury, using data from the United States Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2016 to 2020. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Outcomes included length of stay (LOS), complications, amputations, and 30-day and 90-day unplanned readmissions. Multivariable regression analyses were conducted to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Among an estimated 211,108 hospitalizations nationwide, the weighted prevalence of PAI was 0.38% (95% CI, 0.33%-0.42%). Knee dislocation was the strongest predictor of PAI. After PSM, PAI was associated with higher risks of any medical complication (aOR 2.56, 95% CI 1.88-3.49), respiratory failure or mechanical ventilation (aOR 3.59, 95% CI 2.15-5.98), acute kidney injury (aOR 2.71, 95% CI 1.76-4.19), and any surgical complication (aOR 4.50, 95% CI 3.40-5.97) as well as increased risk of 30-day unplanned readmission (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.21-2.70) and longer LOS (adjusted β 9.15 days, 95% CI 7.57-10.72). CONCLUSIONS: PAI is associated with substantial morbidity and increased healthcare utilization following severe knee trauma, reinforcing the need for comprehensive vascular assessment, particularly in knee dislocation-related injuries. Given the observational nature of this administrative database study, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research

articles.title: Volume vs intensity of physical activity and risk of cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular chronic diseases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While vigorous physical activity (VPA) is known to provide greater health benefits per unit time than moderate activity, the spectrum of these benefits across different chronic diseases and the relative importance of physical activity (PA) intensity vs volume remain unclear. This study examined associations between the proportion of VPA (%VPA) relative to total volume of PA and the incidence of multiple chronic disease outcomes. METHODS: This prospective population-based cohort study included 96,408 participants (mean age 61.9 years, women: 56.3%) with device-measured data (wrist-worn accelerometers) and 375,730 participants (mean age 56.2 years, women: 52.2%) with self-reported PA data (IPAQ) from the UK Biobank. Main outcomes included incidence of eight chronic diseases: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), atrial fibrillation (AFib), type 2 diabetes (T2D), immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), chronic respiratory diseases (CRD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and dementia, as well as all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios and 95% confidence interval. RESULTS: In the device-measured data, non-linear inverse dose-response relationships were observed between %VPA and all outcomes (all P < .001), and these patterns remained consistent across strata of total PA volume. In multivariable models adjusted for total PA volume, participants with >4% VPA had 29%-61% lower risks of these outcomes compared with those with 0% VPA. Joint analyses and population attributable fraction revealed distinct disease-specific patterns: immune-mediated inflammatory diseases showed very strong intensity-dependence with minimal contribution from PA volume (20.3% for intensity vs 1.0% for volume), while MACE (17.8% vs 6.0%), AFib (16.2% vs 5.0%), CRD (21.4% vs 5.6%), and dementia (32.3% vs 8.1%) demonstrated intensity predominance with modest contribution from PA volume, and T2D (26.6% vs 17.7%), MASLD (22.1% vs 16.6%), CKD (23.0% vs 15.3%), and all-cause mortality (31.4% vs 14.2%) showed more balanced contributions from both intensity and volume. CONCLUSIONS: A higher %VPA, independent of total activity volume, is inversely associated with eight major chronic diseases and all-cause mortality. Intensity consistently demonstrated a higher preventive potential than total PA volume. These findings support, whenever possible, prioritizing higher-intensity activities in clinical and public health interventions aimed at preventing non-communicable diseases.

articles.title: Prevalence of Fabry disease GLA variants among patients with parapelvic cysts: a Multicenter Italian Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fabry disease is a rare X-linked disorder characterized by the accumulation of sphingolipids in various vital systems, leading to multiple organ damage. articles.title: Early exercise therapy for acute nephrotic syndrome: a randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In adults with acute nephrotic syndrome (NS), physical function often declines; however, limited evidence on the efficacy and safety of exercise therapy leads to its avoidance due to fears of exacerbated proteinuria and renal deterioration. This study aimed to assess whether early exercise therapy enhances physical function without elevating risks of non-remission or worsening kidney function. METHODS: This single-centre randomised controlled trial enrolled hospitalised adults receiving glucocorticoid therapy for NS. Participants were randomised (1:1) to exercise therapy or standard care. The primary outcome was peak oxygen uptake (peak VO2) at baseline and 6 weeks. The secondary outcome was non-remission at 6 weeks (proteinuria ≥0.3 g/day). Analyses used multiple imputation for missing data, analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline, and modified Poisson regression. RESULTS: Twenty-seven participants were recruited (early intervention, n = 13; standard care, n = 14). Peak VO2 increased significantly in the early exercise group (Δ = 3.45 mL/kg/min; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.22-5.67) but not in the standard care group (Δ = 1.00 mL/kg/min; 95% CI, -1.14 to 3.14). Adjusted between-group difference at 6 weeks was 2.46 mL/kg/min (95% CI, -0.12 to 5.03). Risk ratio for non-remission was 0.673 (95% CI, 0.266-1.703), with no significant intergroup difference. CONCLUSION: Early exercise therapy in acute NS improved exercise tolerance clinically, although the primary outcome between-group difference was not statistically significant. No evidence indicated increased non-remission risk. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN-CTR) (registration number: UMIN000038250; registration date: October 9, 2019).

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of IgA nephropathy with predominant light chain deposition.
articles.abstract: To compare the clinicopathological features, treatment response, and renal outcomes of patients with IgA nephropathy (IgAN) with κ-dominant, κ-λ co-deposition, or λ-dominant light-chain deposition. This retrospective, single-centre cohort study included 105 patients with primary IgAN who underwent their first native-kidney biopsy. Twenty-one patients with κ-dominant deposition were matched to 42 patients with κ-λ co-deposition and 42 patients with λ-dominant deposition based on age, sex, 24-hour urinary protein excretion, and baseline serum creatinine. The final matching ratio was 1:2:2. The primary renal endpoint was a sustained ≥30% increase in serum creatinine from baseline. During a median follow-up of 25 months (IQR, 18-36), 21 patients reached the renal endpoint. Time to treatment response did not differ significantly among the three groups (log-rank p = 0.0707). However, renal progression-free survival differed significantly among the light-chain deposition groups (log-rank p = 0.0046). After adjustment for sex, age, 24-hour urinary protein excretion, and baseline eGFR, a higher κ deposition ratio remained associated with a lower hazard of renal progression (HR [per 1-percentage-point increase] 0.96; 95% CI: 0.94-0.99; p = 0.011). A higher κ light-chain deposition ratio was associated with a lower risk of renal progression in IgAN. κ predominance may be a pathological marker of a distinct and possibly less aggressive immune-complex deposition pattern.

articles.title: Crescents in native kidney biopsies from patients with IgA nephropathy and the risk of recurrence after kidney transplantation: a retrospective cohort study, systematic literature review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is associated with a high risk of kidney failure. Whenever this occurs, the best treatment option is kidney transplantation. IgAN recurrence in the kidney allograft may increase the risk of allograft loss. The association of glomerular crescents in native IgAN is a negative prognostic factor for the progression to kidney failure. The aim of our study was to clarify whether the presence of crescents in native kidney biopsies represents a risk factor for IgAN recurrence in renal allografts. METHODS: The association between glomerular crescents in native kidney biopsies and IgAN recurrence was investigated in IgAN patients who underwent kidney transplantation at Lausanne University Hospital from 2003 to 2019. A systematic literature review was performed in MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science and PMC from inception to November 2025, excluding reviews. Aggregate data were analyzed in a meta-analysis. The overall Risk Ratio (RR) with their corresponding 95% confidence interval (95% CI) was obtained via the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment method, after verifying heterogeneity (I2). Reporting bias was visualized in a funnel plot using STATA. RESULTS: The Lausanne cohort included 63 patients with IgAN who underwent kidney transplantation. We found no association between glomerular crescents in native kidney biopsies and IgA recurrence in the renal allograft. Five additional cohorts were included in our meta-analysis, ultimately merging data from 311 patients, of whom 23% with recurrent IgAN. Crescent prevalence ranged from 12 to 62%, confirming the absence of association with an increased risk of IgAN recurrence [RR 1.53 (95% CI: 0.40-5.90), P = .41]. CONCLUSIONS: Glomerular crescents, especially when present in more than 25% of viable glomeruli, remain an unfavorable prognostic factor for the progression of IgAN to kidney failure; however, they may not represent a risk factor for disease recurrence in renal allografts.

articles.title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

articles.title: Medicare Advantage Enrollment and Access to Kidney Transplant After the 21st Century Cures Act.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Among patients with kidney failure, kidney transplant is associated with better survival and quality of life compared with maintenance dialysis. The 21st Century Cures Act expanded Medicare Advantage eligibility to individuals with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), with limited evidence about access to transplant in Medicare Advantage plans. OBJECTIVE: To compare kidney transplant and wait-listing rates between Medicare Advantage and traditional Medicare beneficiaries with ESKD in the first 3 years after the 21st Century Cures Act. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries aged 18 to 74 years with ESKD who had not received kidney transplant in the prior 3 years from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2023. EXPOSURE: Enrollment in Medicare Advantage vs traditional Medicare. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was kidney transplant. The secondary outcome was incident (new) wait-listing. Models adjusted for demographic characteristics, dual Medicare-Medicaid eligibility, duration of ESKD, socioeconomic status, and hospital referral region. RESULTS: The study population included 630 848 Medicare beneficiaries with ESKD (mean age, 57.9 [SD, 11.0] years; 40.9% female; 35.2% Black; and 19.4% Hispanic). Over 14.8 million person-months, Medicare Advantage beneficiaries had lower transplant rates than those in traditional Medicare (2.51 vs 4.60 per 1000 person-months; adjusted rate ratio [aRR], 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.72). Absolute differences were widest among the youngest beneficiaries (aged 18-44 years) and were stable across calendar years (aRRs: 0.71 [95% CI, 0.68-0.73] in 2021; 0.70 [95% CI, 0.68-0.73] in 2022; and 0.70 [95% CI, 0.68-0.72] in 2023). Incident wait-listing was also lower in Medicare Advantage (3.05 vs 4.64 per 1000 person-months; aRR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.75-0.78). Among beneficiaries wait-listed at baseline or placed on a wait list during observation, Medicare Advantage enrollees had lower transplant rates (16.59 vs 20.85 per 1000 person-months; aRR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.90-0.92). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In the first 3 years following the 21st Century Cures Act, Medicare Advantage beneficiaries with ESKD had substantially lower transplant and wait-listing rates than traditional Medicare beneficiaries. Policy oversight may be needed to monitor access for this critical, high-value treatment for kidney failure among the rapidly growing Medicare Advantage population.

articles.title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

articles.title: HbA1c and LDL-C Time in Therapeutic Range: A Study on All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Whether long-term attainment of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets improves prognosis in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear. We used time in therapeutic range (TTR) to quantify sustained glycemic and lipid control and examined its association, and interaction, with all-cause mortality. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study, based on the Tianjin Health Big Data Platform, included 2005 older (≥65 years) and 5973 younger (<65 years) adults with T2DM-CKD. HbA1c-TTR (target <7.0%) and LDL-TTR (target <1.8 mmol/L) were calculated using the Rosendaal method. After Cox-LASSO covariate selection, multivariable Cox models with and without an interaction term were built, supplemented by RCS, subgroup analyses, and landmark and time-varying covariate sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 4.56 years, 211 older adults (10.5%) died. Without an interaction term, LDL-TTR (per 10-percentage-point increase) was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.934, P=0.003), while HbA1c-TTR was not (HR 0.983, P=0.459); with the interaction term, the HbA1c-TTR × LDL-TTR interaction was significant (HR 1.016, P=0.006). Adjusted RCS showed a significant nonlinear association for LDL-TTR (P nonlinear=0.020) but not for HbA1c-TTR overall (P=0.231). In the younger cohort, both main effects were significant, but the interaction was not (P=0.124). The interaction remained significant in the time-varying covariate model (HR 1.013, P=0.019) but not in the landmark analysis or under the alternative 6.5-8.0% HbA1c definition, under which LDL-TTR's main effect remained significant. CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with T2DM and CKD, higher LDL-TTR was independently associated with lower mortality, and a significant HbA1c-TTR × LDL-TTR interaction suggested that the inverse association of one TTR measure with mortality was attenuated at higher levels of the other. This interaction was absent in the younger cohort and under an alternative HbA1c target (6.5-8.0%), and was inconsistent across sensitivity analyses (significant with time-varying covariates, HR 1.013, P=0.019; non-significant in a landmark analysis, P=0.968). These exploratory findings do not support changing current management targets and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Predictors of physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify predictors of physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. Participants underwent assessment of physical performance using the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), the 60-second sit-to-stand (60s-STS) test, handgrip strength, bone mineral density (BMD) by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), and clinical and laboratory variables. Participants were classified according to changes in SPPB score between baseline and follow-up. The minimal detectable change (MDC) of the SPPB was used as the criterion for defining physical performance decline. Statistical analysis included Student's t-test, the Mann-Whitney test, and chi-square tests. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable penalized logistic regression with Firth correction were used to identify predictors of physical performance decline. RESULTS: Of the 103 participants, 18 (17.5%) experienced physical performance decline after a mean follow-up of 18.6 ± 10.1 months. Compared with those who maintained physical performance, participants with physical performance decline were older and had lower total and femoral bone mineral density and poorer performance on the 60s-STS test at baseline. In the multivariable penalized logistic regression analysis, lower femoral BMD (OR: 0.997; 95% CI: 0.991-0.999) and longer hemodialysis vintage (OR: 1.009; 95% CI: 1.001-1.039) were independently associated with physical performance decline. CONCLUSION: This prospective study showed that lower femoral bone mineral density and longer hemodialysis vintage were independently associated with physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. These findings underscore the potential value of longitudinal physical performance assessment and may help identify patients at greater risk of functional decline.

articles.title: Anti-PLA2R antibody levels are associated with thromboembolism risk in individuals with membranous nephropathy and hypoalbuminemia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies to evaluate markers of thrombotic risk in individuals with high-risk membranous nephropathy (MN) are needed. We hypothesized that high anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) titers at the time of severe hypoalbuminemia, reflecting ongoing immunologic disease activity, may be associated with a higher risk of thrombotic complications. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of individuals with membranous nephropathy and serum albumin <2.5 g/dL and evaluated risk factors for first thrombotic events. RESULTS: Sixty-seven individuals met the inclusion criteria. Median serum creatinine was 1.2 mg/dL (Interquartile range [IQR] 0.9-1.6), median urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) was 11.9 g/g (IQR 8.5-16.5), and median nadir serum albumin level was 1.9 g/dL (IQR 1.6-2.2). Twenty-four individuals (36%) received no thromboprophylaxis, 20 (30%) received prophylaxis with only antiplatelets, and 23 (34%) received anticoagulation prophylaxis. Thrombotic events occurred in 11 individuals (16%) with incidence rates of 0.11, 0.10, and 0.02 per person-year in the no prophylaxis, antiplatelet, and anticoagulation groups, respectively. In individuals with anti-PLA2R antibody-positive MN who did not receive anticoagulation thromboprophylaxis, higher anti-PLA2R antibody levels were associated with a higher risk of developing thrombotic complications (adjusted Hazard Ratio [HR] = 1.51 per 10 RU/mL increase in PLA2R, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.10-2.09, P = .012) after adjusting for serum albumin nadir and age. CONCLUSIONS: Higher anti-PLA2R antibody levels at the time of hypoalbuminemia are associated with a higher risk of thrombotic complications in individuals with anti-PLA2R-positive MN.

articles.title: Rifampicin-soaked versus bovine prostheses in the management of aortic graft infections: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic vascular graft and endograft infections (aortic VGEI) remain a rare but life-threatening complication following aortic reconstruction. This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction. Patients received either a bovine pericardial graft (n=21) or a rifampicin-soaked Dacron prosthesis (n=41). Survival, treatment failure, perioperative variables, and microbiology were analyzed. RESULTS: Patients in the bovine and rifampicin groups were comparable in terms of age (72.57 vs. 73.58 years, p = 0.685) and sex distribution (85.71% vs. 73.17% male, p = 0.346). BMI, preoperative dialysis, and aortic clamping time were higher in the bovine group. Four treatment failures, defined as persistent or recurrent infection of the reconstructed aortic segment, occurred during follow-up; all were observed after reconstruction with rifampicin-soaked Dacron (4/41, 9.8%), whereas no treatment failure occurred in the bovine pericardial group (0/21). In-hospital mortality was comparable between groups (n=3:14.3% vs. n=8: 19.5%, p = 0.735). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in survival (p = 0.256) or treatment failure rate (p = 0.833). Candida spp. were the most frequent pathogens (27.8%) and significantly associated with secondary aorto-enteric fistula (p=0.003). CONCLUSION: Survival and treatment failure rates were comparable, with a trend toward fewer infection-related complications after bovine pericardial grafting. Despite use in more complex cases, bovine grafts may represent a promising biological alternative.
